key.name: focus-window-left
key.summary: Focus the window on the left

key.name: focus-window-right
key.summary: Focus the window on the right

key.name: focus-window-up
key.summary: Focus the window above

key.name: focus-window-down
key.summary: Focus the window below

key.name: move-window-left
key.summary: Swap with the window on the left (or move to the monitor there)

key.name: move-window-right
key.summary: Swap with the window on the right (or move to the monitor there)

key.name: move-window-up
key.summary: Swap with the window above

key.name: move-window-down
key.summary: Swap with the window below

key.name: untile-window
key.summary: Float the window, or tile it again

key.name: cycle-layouts
key.summary: Next layout: main left, main on top

key.name: span-window-all-tiles
key.summary: Monocle: every window fills the work area, or back

key.name: shrink-main
key.summary: Narrower main area

key.name: grow-main
key.summary: Wider main area

key.name: window-to-monitor-left
key.summary: Move the window to the monitor on the left

key.name: window-to-monitor-right
key.summary: Move the window to the monitor on the right

key.name: window-to-monitor-up
key.summary: Move the window to the monitor above

key.name: window-to-monitor-down
key.summary: Move the window to the monitor below

key.name: main-ratio
key.summary: Share of the main area (1 = whole work area)
key.description: Default for a workspace and monitor whose split was not changed since login.

key.name: border-width
key.summary: Border around every tiled window, in pixels (0 = none)
key.description: Drawn inside the window's tile, so windows never overlap it; the focused window's border has border-color, the others inactive-border-color.

key.name: border-color
key.summary: Border colour of the focused window (CSS colour; kit-desk theme sets the theme's accent)

key.name: inactive-border-color
key.summary: Border colour of the other tiled windows (CSS colour)

key.name: float-classes
key.summary: WM classes that always float (zenity: the kit's own menus, centred like Omarchy's)
